correctness.rationale: For each A in (0,1/2], compactness yields a maximizing triangle. Fixing ordinate coordinates and signed double area gives a 2-dimensional affine kernel of horizontal perturbations; moving a triangle with horizontal span <1 wholly into the square leaves a nontranslation feasible direction along which the perimeter is strictly convex, contradicting interior maximality. The same holds vertically. Thus normalized vertex coordinate extrema are 0 and 1. Coordinate orders reduce exactly to diagonal-edge Case I and the no-opposite-corner Case II. In I strict convexity along |s-t|=2A forces side endpoints, giving M(A). In II write q=st=1-2A and p=s+t in [2sqrt q,1+q]. The closed expression U(p)+V(p) is strictly increasing for q>=1/4 (p>=1) and strictly convex for q<1/4 (U second derivative positive since c=1-q>3/4, V second derivative positive); hence extrema at endpoints. Direct comparison shows p=1+q wins for 0<q<1/4; at q=0 endpoints represent identical three-corner equality orbits. Derivatives Mprime>0 and Mdoubleprime>0 and dihedral orbit counting yield 8 maximizers for 0<A<1/2, 4 at A=1/2. Independently checked rational equality witnesses and several Case-II inequalities; finite tests corroborate the continuum argument.
